I have even tried ChatGPT, without success!

And there is no way to revert to the previous version !!!!!

Please do something NOW, or it is, regrettably, goodbye Thunderbird!

title: Drag-and-drop email export to Windows Explorer no longer works in Thunderbird 153.0.2esr
creator: samsungchobg
content:
Environment:

Thunderbird: 153.0.2esr (64-bit) Operating system: Windows Occurs with multiple email accounts Reproduced on two different computers running the same Thunderbird version

Description:

After updating Thunderbird to version 153.0.2esr, released on 4 August 2026, emails can no longer be dragged and dropped from Thunderbird to the Windows Desktop or any folder in Windows Explorer.

The problem occurs with all tested email accounts and folders. It has been reproduced independently on two different Windows computers using the same Thunderbird version.

Saving an email manually with Ctrl+S works correctly and creates the .eml file. Normal drag-and-drop between folders in Windows Explorer also works. Only dragging an email from Thunderbird to Windows Explorer fails.

The issue also appears to affect third-party applications that use Thunderbird to create or send emails automatically.

Steps to reproduce:

Open Thunderbird 153.0.2esr on Windows. Select an email in any account or folder. Drag the email to the Desktop or another folder in Windows Explorer. Release the mouse button.

Actual result:

The email is not copied or saved to the selected Windows folder.

Expected result:

Thunderbird should export the email as an .eml file in the selected folder.

Additional information:

Ctrl+S successfully saves the same email. The issue affects every tested email account. Thunderbird extensions were disabled, but the problem remained. Thunderbird Troubleshoot Mode did not resolve the issue. Restarting Thunderbird, Windows Explorer and Windows did not resolve it. Thunderbird and Windows Explorer are not running with different elevation levels. The problem was reproduced on a second computer after installing the same Thunderbird version. No relevant error is shown in Thunderbird’s Error Console when the drag-and-drop operation fails. The issue was not present before the recent Thunderbird update.

This appears to be a regression in Thunderbird 153.0.2esr affecting email export through drag-and-drop and possibly Thunderbird’s integration with external applications.

title: Hotmail personal account: IMAP OAuth2 works but SMTP OAuth2 fails with message: 535 5.7.139 “SmtpClientAuthentication is disabled for the Mailbox”
creator: joncoffey68
content:
I am assisting an elderly user with a personal @hotmail.com account that receives email successfully in Thunderbird but cannot send. I have confirmed they can send and receive emails from their online outlook.com portal. The user's computer setup is as follows:

  • Windows 11 (with latest updates).
  • Thunderbird 153.0.2 (64-bit).
  • A personal @hotmail.com account with the following server configurations: 
  -> Incoming IMAP: outlook.office365.com, port 993, SSL/TLS, OAuth2, and   -> Outgoing SMTP: smtp-mail.outlook.com, port 587, STARTTLS, OAuth2.

Thunderbird successfully authenticates to Microsoft using OAuth2 for incoming email. However, when Thunderbird attempts outgoing email authentication, Microsoft's SMTP server rejects the authentication. The Error Console in Thunderbird records this message: "535 5.7.139 Authentication unsuccessful, SmtpClientAuthentication is disabled for the Mailbox."

-> Refer to attached image: "Thunderbird Error Console_20260811.jpg". -> I am able to provide a short screen recording demonstrating the failure if needed.

To try and resolve the above, I completed the following actions:

  1. Confirmed Thunderbird is current (153.0.2).
  2. Confirmed SMTP is configured for OAuth2 rather than Normal Password.
  3. Confirmed port 587 and STARTTLS.
  4. Re-authorised the Microsoft account/OAuth connection.
  5. Confirmed IMAP OAuth2 works.
  6. Confirmed Outlook.com webmail can send successfully.
  7. Reviewed Mozilla's current “Microsoft OAuth Authentication and Thunderbird in 2026” guidance, including the section covering cases where IMAP/POP works but SMTP does not.
  8. Captured the SMTP failure in Thunderbird's Error Console.

However nothing worked, so I raised the matter with Microsoft support and eventually had the matter referred to their Tier 2 team. The Microsoft case number is: 7107041963.

Microsoft Support confirmed that for a personal Outlook.com/Hotmail account there is no user-accessible mailbox-level SMTP AUTH setting, and advised that SMTP is enabled by default for supported clients. However, because sending from Outlook.com webmail works, Microsoft Tier 2 declined to investigate the SMTP server response further and directed me to Thunderbird support.

I am able to provide a copy of the chat transcript if needed.

In any event, the TLDR version IMAP works using OAuth2, but SMTP using OAuth2 fails because Microsoft's SMTP server reports SmtpClientAuthentication is disabled for the Mailbox. Microsoft Tier 2 has referred the issue to Thunderbird support.

Questions:

  1. Is this a known current issue affecting personal Outlook.com/Hotmail accounts using Thunderbird?
  2. Is 535 5.7.139 SmtpClientAuthentication is disabled for the Mailbox known to occur with Thunderbird OAuth2 even though IMAP OAuth2 succeeds?
  3. Is there a current Thunderbird-side workaround or alternative SMTP server/configuration recommended for personal Hotmail accounts?
  4. Would changing the SMTP server from smtp-mail.outlook.com to smtp.office365.com be appropriate for a personal Hotmail account in Thunderbird 153, or should the current Microsoft-documented server be retained?

-> I note there appears to be conflicting advice on this point in previous support threads.

  1. Given that IMAP OAuth2 authentication succeeds for the same Microsoft account, does this indicate that Thunderbird's Microsoft OAuth authorisation itself is functioning correctly, or could SMTP require a separate permission/token that may be failing?
  2. Are there any additional Thunderbird logs or diagnostics I can provide that would help resolve this matter?

Disclosure: I used ChatGPT to help organise my troubleshooting notes and technical details for this post. The troubleshooting, observations and diagnostic information described above are from my own work on the affected PC.

title: BUGZILLA bug feedback uses AMAZON and its reporting IP address is getting bounced
creator: td47
content:
It seems it is because BUGZILLA uses the AMAZON'S service, but there is now a RANGE of IP addresses that have been blocked, and BUGZILLA have been caught up in this mess. Please let me know which board I can use to report/ask about this issue, if it is no on here..

Here is the issue research (NOTE: I have emailed the BMO_MODS email several times, but had NO RESPONSE, so want to check if others have this issue):

Based on the error message you're receiving, Microsoft is blocking emails from your IP address because it appears on their block list. This is a Microsoft-specific issue rather than an AWS problem. When you receive a 550 5.7.1 error with the S3150 code from Microsoft domains (Hotmail, Outlook), it means Microsoft's filtering systems have identified your IP address as a source of problematic traffic. Even though you're using a managed dedicated IP and haven't intentionally violated any policies, there are several reasons this could occur: The IP address may have a poor reputation due to previous usage by another customer, spam complaints from recipients, high bounce rates, or sending patterns that Microsoft's algorithms flag as suspicious. Sometimes legitimate senders get caught in these filters. To resolve this issue, you should:
  • Contact Microsoft directly using the troubleshooting link provided in the error message (mail.live.com/mail/troubleshooting.aspx) to request delisting
  • Review your email sending practices to ensure you're following best practices (proper authentication, low complaint rates, engaged recipient lists)
  • Consider contacting AWS Support to discuss your dedicated IP's reputation and whether a new IP might be warranted
  • Ensure your SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records are properly configured Microsoft maintains their own independent block lists and reputation systems, so even with AWS's managed infrastructure, you may need to work directly with Microsoft to resolve deliverability issues to their domains.

title: IMAP/SMTP server connected, but receives and send fails
creator: manishchawla619
content:
1. Thunderbird connects to my IMAP/SMTP server but neither receives nor sends mail

I am having a problem with Thunderbird on Windows with a custom-domain email account hosted by Advika Web.

      1. Account

Email address: `connect@synergyappstudio.com`

Mail hosting provider: Advika Web

The mailbox and password are confirmed to be valid because I can successfully log in to the provider's webmail using the same email address and password.

      1. Server settings provided by the hosting provider

Incoming IMAP:

  • Server: `mail.synergyappstudio.com`
  • Port: `993`
  • Connection security: SSL/TLS
  • Authentication: Normal password
  • Username: `connect@synergyappstudio.com`

Outgoing SMTP:

  • Server: `mail.synergyappstudio.com`
  • Port: `465`
  • Connection security: SSL/TLS
  • Authentication: Normal password
  • Username: `connect@synergyappstudio.com`
      1. What happens in Thunderbird

Thunderbird shows:

> Connected to mail.synergyappstudio.com

However, incoming messages are not downloaded and outgoing messages cannot be sent.

The SMTP error I received was:

> The connection to Outgoing server (SMTP) mail.synergyappstudio.com timed out.

      1. Connectivity tests

I tested the server from Windows PowerShell.

Port 993:

`Test-NetConnection mail.synergyappstudio.com -Port 993`

Result:

> RemoteAddress: 103.69.196.146 > RemotePort: 993 > TcpTestSucceeded: True

Port 465:

`Test-NetConnection mail.synergyappstudio.com -Port 465`

Result:

> RemoteAddress: 103.69.196.146 > RemotePort: 465 > TcpTestSucceeded: True

Therefore, both TCP ports are reachable from my computer.

      1. TLS tests

I also tested the actual TLS handshake rather than just TCP connectivity.

TLS 1.2 against IMAP 993 failed with:

> Unable to read data from the transport connection: An existing connection was forcibly closed by the remote host.

TLS 1.0 against IMAP 993 produced the same result:

> Unable to read data from the transport connection: An existing connection was forcibly closed by the remote host.

I also tested the TLS handshake against SMTP 465 and received the same "connection was forcibly closed by the remote host" result.

      1. Comparison with Outlook

There is an important comparison:

The same mailbox **successfully connects and authenticates in Classic Outlook** using the same server and credentials.

However, I am using Microsoft Office Home & Student, so Classic Outlook is not available to me as a practical permanent solution for this business email account.

Microsoft's **New Outlook** also fails to add the account and displays:

> Sign in failed. Please try again in a few minutes. You may need an app password.

The mailbox does not use Microsoft 365 authentication. It is a conventional hosting-provider IMAP/SMTP mailbox.

      1. Thunderbird troubleshooting already attempted

I have:

  • Confirmed the password works through webmail.
  • Confirmed the supplied IMAP/SMTP server names.
  • Confirmed ports 993 and 465 are reachable.
  • Confirmed SSL/TLS settings.
  • Used Normal Password authentication.
  • Used the full email address as the username.
  • Tried Thunderbird with the supplied IMAP/SMTP settings.
  • Reduced **Maximum number of server connections to cache** from the default 5 to 3 and then to 1. This did not resolve the problem.
  • Restarted Thunderbird after changing the connection-cache setting.
  • Tried Thunderbird's connection logging, but the generated log files remained 0 KB, so no useful log was produced.
      1. Additional observation

Thunderbird displays "Connected to mail.synergyappstudio.com", but the account does not actually synchronize incoming mail.

The provider's webmail works normally, and Classic Outlook works with the same mailbox.

      1. What I would like help determining

Could you please help determine whether this is:

1. A Thunderbird IMAP/SMTP compatibility issue with this particular mail server; 2. A TLS negotiation issue; 3. A Thunderbird configuration/profile issue; 4. A Windows/security-software interaction; or 5. Something specific to the mail server's IMAP/SMTP implementation?

In particular, I would like to understand why Thunderbird can establish the connection but cannot complete the IMAP/SMTP communication, while Classic Outlook works with the same server, ports and credentials.

I can provide Thunderbird version information, Troubleshooting Information, screenshots of the account configuration, or any additional diagnostic information you need.
